title: Health Assessment of Higher Education by IEW-TOPSIS

context_sources.name: OECD Benchmarking Higher Education System Performance
Chilean Ministry of Education, mifuturo
context_sources.role: Time series for the grey model

limitations: All formulas on pages 12-13 are private-use glyphs. Reconstructed as standard IEW-TOPSIS.
Running headers leak into the text layer, and the file is not valid UTF-8.
Shannon's paper is dated 1984. Assumption 9 in the list is the public-private claim, while the text cites hypothesis 9 for the caliber claim, which is assumption 10 in the printed list.
The entropy-weight prose reverses the usual story.

tasks: Define and measure the health of a higher education system
Apply it and choose a country with room to improve
Set an achievable vision from national conditions
Discuss the impact on real groups

section_map.summary: Two aspects of health, IEW-TOPSIS, Chile chosen, grey check, policy called insufficient.
Pulse and temperature metaphor, premium against rising burden, ten assumptions.
Strength is not health. Coverage, fairness, achievement against input, output, efficiency.
Two indicator tables, entropy weights, closeness, grades, 21 countries.
One indicator at a time. Score barely moves, so policy must move several.
Chile 0.279 and 0.734. Vision equals the mean of four stable indicators. GM(1,1) misses it.
Four policies, a timetable, five affected groups. Rescored Chile reaches 0.445.
Inverse scatter treated as confirmation. Six weaknesses, including the model's own.

contributions.summary: Health is not strength. Performance and potential are scored separately and expected to move in opposite directions.
A mean is used as a target only after its coefficient of variation is shown to be small.
The authors report that their own policy leaves Chile short of healthy.

dependency_graph.handoff: The master-ratio indicator and its 21-country mean, 0.363 against Chile's 0.115, are the target the grey forecast is shown to miss

assumptions.summary: Quantity can compensate a quality gap that is not too wide. Coverage cannot be replaced by good basic education.
Public institutions pursue justice, private ones efficiency. Unfairness comes from income and status.
Without a strong policy, indicators move slowly, so a missing year can be borrowed from within two years. A strong policy needs the authority, the legislature and the executive.
Shocks are excluded. Different statistical calibers share a trend.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: 21 OECD countries, 2016. Positive and negative indicators scaled separately. One negative indicator, the student-teacher ratio.

models.summary: IEW-TOPSIS run twice, ten indicators for performance and eleven for potential.
GM(1,1) on Chile's master ratio, 2007-2018, forecast to 2028.

verification.summary: Sensitivity: one indicator moved at a time barely shifts the score.
Substituting the four vision values lifts Chile from 0.279497 to 0.444658.
The two scores scatter inversely, with a double-high and a double-low corner left unfitted.

results_trace.summary: Performance: 11 countries above 0.5, only 2 above 0.6. Slovak Republic 0.639816, Israel 0.264504.
Chile: performance 0.279497, potential 0.73439, the largest gap of the 21.
Vision for four low-variation indicators: means 0.363, 0.550, 71.2, 1.857 against Chile's 0.115, 0.282, 15.4, 0.3.
Policy rescoring: 0.279497 to 0.444658. Authors call this short of healthy.

writing_logic.summary: Summary states the selection rule before the country: huge potential and poor performance. Chile is the country that satisfies it.
Each indicator is a row with an abbreviation, a definition and a data-processing note. The table is the argument.
Verification is a picture plus a mechanism plus a concession. The inverse holds roughly, the corners violate it, and they decline to fit.

language_observations.summary: 'Pulse and temperature' for the two models. Used twice, then dropped. The metaphor is a label, not a system.
The athlete analogy does one job: a strong body can still be in pain. It licenses throwing out level indicators such as Nobel counts.
One sentence gives the whole hierarchy: coverage is the cornerstone of fairness, fairness the basis of achievement.
They refuse to use a mean until they have defended it with the coefficient of variation.
'Of course ... beyond the scope of our argument, so we will not repeat them' declines a task cleanly.
They explain why the improved score is still mediocre before anyone can attack it.
They notice the outliers, say what a careful fit would do, and then say they will not do it. The stopping is the move.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: Rejecting a flattering indicator, the Nobel count, with two reasons makes the remaining indicators look chosen rather than gathered.
A target set at the mean, and only for low-variation indicators, is modest and defensible. The modesty is the credibility.
Calling the policy insufficient in the summary is unusual and expensive. It is also the sentence that makes the rest believable.

weaknesses.summary: Authors: entropy cannot drop dimensions, and it misbehaves when a value barely moves or jumps.
Authors: the grey series is not smooth enough, input and output are not coordinated, and only some factors were used.
The entropy rationale is reversed, the source year is wrong, and the weights are never printed.

independent_extensions.summary: Print the entropy weights and recompute the two rankings.
Fit the inverse relation after reporting, rather than deleting, the double-high and double-low countries.

candidate_rule_impacts.summary: A system scored on its present state and on its room to change, with the two expected to oppose each other.
Policies aimed at the indicators below a defended mean, with a crisis response separated from the structural reform.

unresolved_questions.question: What are the entropy weights, and do they agree with the reversed prose?
What was the level-ratio test statistic, and how large is the forecast error?
